About the Trending chart

This board is the last seven days of real downloads on AnkerGames, and nothing else. Downloads are counted on a rolling basis, so the order can move any day, and every position is measured against a weekly checkpoint. That is what tells you which games are climbing, which are slipping, which have just broken in and which have fallen off the board entirely.

Games marked "Steam agrees" are trending on Steam this week as well, so the surge is not a quirk of our own traffic. Every game here is free, pre-installed and ready to download, with no launcher needed.

Frequently asked questions

Every game on the board is ranked by how many times it was actually downloaded here in the last seven days, counted on a rolling basis. Those positions are then compared against a weekly checkpoint to show what climbed, what slipped and what is new. The numbers are real download counts recorded on this site, not estimates or third-party sampling.

Top Games ranks by all-time downloads, so it changes slowly and tells you what always wins. Trending only cares about the last seven days and about movement, so it tells you what changed. A game can be No.1 on Top and going nowhere on Trending.

It is a game that has been in the library for a long time and has suddenly broken onto the board. Nobody just uploaded it: players found it again on their own. A game marked "Just Added" is the opposite, a recent upload charting in its first weeks.

Downloads are counted over a rolling seven-day window, so the order can shift any day. The comparison points, which decide what counts as climbing, slipping or new, are recorded once a week, and each game's peak position and weeks on the board carry over.
